independent_mathematical_challenges.reason: The source premises and literal Eq22 discharge n>1, s>=2, 0<q<1, 0<r<1, lambda>0, 1-r^2>0 and C>0 internally. No positivity witness is exported.
The chosen r=(1-1/n)q and lambda=[4ns+(s-1)^2]/[8n(n-1)] are shared by Eq20 and Eq24; Eq20's lambda>=0 condition is explicitly discharged from the strictly positive chosen tilt.
Eq24 retains (-1)^n. The gap bridge removes it only inside abs, using abs((-1)^n)=1 and positive remaining factors. Odd n gives negative H; no H>=0 assumption or parity restriction is introduced.
Both Eq24 and the convexity estimate use real n/2. The graph explicitly covers odd n, the nonnegative base and n/2>=1; natural-number truncation is excluded.

The exact identity n(1-r^2)=4ns/(s+1)^2+q^2(2-1/n) and upper bound C are retained. Both denominators are positive, so inversion gives the correct lower-bound direction. The graph names C as D; this is a notation change only.

Eq20 AND the absolute form of Eq24 AND the real half-power lower bound AND the denominator upper bound imply the actual-law rational TV bound. A scalar Eq24 value by itself is not treated as actual TV.
